The reasonable setting of guides can directly improve the evacuation capacity in the sub-
way station. The important role of guide assignment scheme and evacuation path planning
of guided passengers is particularly prominent. Considering the distribution of passengers
in the station, one contribution is that an assignment scheme of the initial number and lo-
cation of guides is ﬁrstly established based on Gaussian mixture model and cost function
method, so as to increase the guidance range and reduce the waste of human resources.
Another contribution is that a multi-objective optimization model is developed for guide
path planning and NSGA-II method is used to ﬁnd the optimal solution, which could help
avoiding the evacuation bottlenecks in advance. Massmotion embedded with social force
model and minimum cost model is adopted to simulate the movement of people, which
is veriﬁed by the independent sample t-test in this paper. Evacuation experiments under
the random distribution of passengers are carried out to demonstrate the signiﬁcance of
the proposed guidance method. The results indicate that the total evacuation eﬃciency
can be improved by about 13% in the scenario with guides, and the passengers’ choice of
stairs/escalators is more balanced. Moreover, passengers induced by different guides can
avoid reaching the same evacuation node at the same time window, which alleviates the
pressure of nodes. The results could provide theoretical support for passenger safety man-
agement and even improve the service level of stations.

1. Introduction
Subway, as the main body of urban rail transit, is becoming more and more popular for its characteristics of saving
road land, no traﬃc interference, energy conservation and environmental protection. Take China as an example, subway
lines had reached 7209.7 km with a cumulative passenger volume of 23.69 billion by the end of 2021 [1] . Different from
other modes of transportation, the subway is built in a closed underground with centralized equipments in the station and
large passenger ﬂows. The safety management of passengers in the conﬁned space is particularly prominent [2] . In recent
years, accidents occurred frequently in subway stations all over the world. For example, the severe rainstorm in Zhengzhou,
China led to the siege of subway train by ﬂood in July 2020, resulting in 14 deaths [3] . The aging line led to a ﬁre of Moscow

subway station in Russia in June 2013, resulting in 52 injuries [4] . The Daegu subway station in Korea suffered ﬁres on arson
in February 2003, resulting in 198 deaths and more than 146 injuries [5] . If there is no reasonable and effective evacuation
guidance strategy, it is very diﬃcult for passengers to escape quickly from the subway station [6] . When analyzing the causes
of casualties, it is found that in addition to the accident itself, the stampede caused by the accident is another important
cause of injury and even death [7] . Passengers usually have adverse emotions such as anxiety, tension and even fear in
an emergency which are easy to cause crowd confusion and lead to secondary injuries such as stampede [8] .The advance
planning of passenger evacuation path and guidance strategy in case of emergency can signiﬁcantly improve the evacuation
eﬃciency of passengers in the station, which has important research signiﬁcance and practical value.
The evacuation guidance methods commonly used in subway stations can be divided into substance guidance [9] and
human guidance [10] . Substance guidance is to lead passengers to evacuate by the aid of ﬁxed signage [11] . Human guidance
is to guide the evacuation direction or lead passengers to evacuate directly. Compared with substance guidance, human
guidance is more ﬂexible and can give passengers a higher sense of security. When the passenger density is moderate, the
evacuation eﬃciency will be higher in the evacuation scene under guides [12,13] . In recent years, more and more scholars
begin to pay attention to the problem of pedestrian evacuation under guides [14] , mainly focusing on the macroscopic and
microscopic evacuation rules of pedestrians under guides [15,16] , the guide assignment scheme [17] and the exit choice of
guides [18] . However, the research on guidance strategy including both guide assignment and path planning which could
directly affect evacuation eﬃciency is less and not in-depth, it is worthy of our follow-up discussion.
The novelty and main contributions can be summarized as: (i) This paper puts forward an initial assignment scheme of
guides based on Gaussian mixture model and cost function method, considering the factors of passenger confusion index,
the number of guides, labor cost and balance of passenger quantity led by each guide. It could make the arrangement of
guides more reasonable. It is worth mentioning that the confusion index is creatively introduced into the cost function.
(ii) A multi-objective path optimization model for guided passengers considering evacuation time and path congestion is
proposed, which can effectively determine the key nodes on the path. The time target is to minimize the evacuation time
of the last guide, which can ensure more passengers to evacuate safely in a certain period of time. The method could also
avoid the occurrence of local optimization. This is the main innovation of this paper. (iii) Taking a subway station as a
veriﬁcation example, the proposed method can ensure the safe travel of more passengers, thereby signiﬁcantly improving
the evacuation eﬃciency.
The rest of this paper is organized as follows. Section 2 reviews and analyzes the existing results in the research direction
of this paper. The social force model, the minimum cost model, the assignment scheme of guides, and the guide path
planning model are given, and the NSGA-II algorithm is used to solve the model in Section 3 . In Section 4 , the simulation
scene is brieﬂy introduced, and the rationality of the social force model and the minimum cost model is veriﬁed based on
the collected ﬁeld data. The evacuation ability of passengers under guides is analyzed in Section 5 . Section 6 summarizes
the key results of this paper.
2. Literature review
Generally, the real-life experiment [19–21] is dangerous and involves ethics, the research on evacuation behavior induced
by guides is often carried out based on simulation model [22,23] . The frequently used models to study pedestrian evacuation
mainly include social force model [2,24–30] , cellular automata model [31–36] and ﬂuid/gas dynamics model [37–39] . The
microscopic cellular automata model meshes the pedestrian movement area, and pedestrians move in the grid according
to speciﬁc transition probabilities. This model is simple to calculate, but the pedestrian movement direction is limited by
the grid. The macroscopic ﬂuid/gas dynamics model compares the crowd to ﬂuid/gas. It has a relatively small amount of
calculation, but can not characterize the individual behavior habits. The social force model abstracts the inﬂuence of people-
people and people-obstacle into forces and describes pedestrian movements through force modeling, which can better reﬂect
the self-organization phenomenon and individual travel characteristics. Therefore, this paper selects the social force model
as the basic movement model to drive passengers in the subway station.
The evacuation eﬃciency of passengers is closely related to the professional level of guides. For example, the guidance
ability of specially trained guides is much stronger than that of untrained guides [25] . Generally, there are two guidance
methods for the guide, namely adsorption guidance and directional guidance [40] . Adsorption guidance is that a small num-
ber of pedestrians are induced by guides, and then a sound through this part of a small number of guided pedestrians is
made to attract the attention of other pedestrians during escape. However, it is usually unpredictable and diﬃcult to judge
the following state of pedestrians. Directional guidance is to transmit evacuation information through sound, screen, etc.,
but the guidance effect is diﬃcult to model. In order to overcome these diﬃculties, Yang et al. [13] assigned the guides to
the crowd centers and led the surrounding people to evacuate directly. This guidance method can induce the crowd more
effectively. The passengers have the process of receiving, recognizing and responding to the information when the guide in
the station transmits the evacuation path information [41] , so the transmission mode of the information could also affect
the evacuation ability.
The assignment scheme of guides is mainly reﬂected in the optimization of the number and location of guides, which
plays a vital role in improving the evacuation eﬃciency [42] . According to the federal guidelines, when the ratio of the
number of guides to the number of guided pedestrians reaches 1:20, the evacuation effect could achieve the best [27,43] .
Pelechano and Badler [25] believed that this best ratio was 1:9. Hou et al. [26] believed that when the number of guides

was equal to the number of exits, the guidance effect was the best. The existing research does not clearly give a uniﬁed
proportional value, but only a lower bound of the guide quantity required [44] . Generally, the evacuation eﬃciency under
the uniform distribution of guides is higher than that under the non-uniform distribution [42] . However, the differences in
passenger density at different locations and security needs are not considered when determining the distribution of guides.
It could lead to local excessive congestion and even stampede accidents when a guide leads too many pedestrians. Therefore,
it is very necessary to have further discussions on the assignment of guides.
The path planning of the guide is another important decision-making factor affecting the evacuation eﬃciency. There are
few studies on the problem of guide path planning according to our limited investigation. Methods such as random utility
theory [42] and game theory [45] are often used to determine the exit of the guide, but they can not give the speciﬁc path
of the guide to that exit. The frequently used A ∗algorithm needs to determine the weight value of factors affecting path
selection, and it even could cause a lot of space consumption when the target point is not reachable [2] . Many existing
studies take evacuation time as the only target of path planning, nevertheless, multiple targets should be considered at the
same time such as congestion degree and risk degree [46] .
At present, it is found that there are few studies considering both initial assignment of the guide and path planning at
the same time [18] . Zhang and Jia [47] used the maximum coverage method to model the initial assignment of guides in
simple scenarios, and studied the exit decision making. Among which, pedestrian movement was based on cellular automata
model, it did not take into account the heterogeneity of the crowd and the motion direction of pedestrian was also limited
to the lattice space. Meanwhile, only the target exit of the guide was determined, and the speciﬁc path to the exit was not
planned. Zhou et al. [2] also obtained the guide assignment scheme through the maximum coverage method, and planned
the guide’s evacuation path by considering the number of guides, the total evacuation time and the safety cost. However, it
only considered whether the passengers were induced by a guide and the labor cost in the process of formulating the guide
assignment scheme, ignoring the inﬂuence of passenger confusion index and the balance of the number of passengers led by
the guides. It may result in the excessive number of passengers following a guide. In addition, Ref. [42] only simply added
the three objective functions as the total objective, it was easy to cause the deviation of a certain objective value from the
optimal solution to be too large, such as the evacuation time was too long even if the total target value was optimal.
The established initial assignment model of the guide in this paper comprehensively considers the factors of passenger
confusion index, the number of guides, labor cost and the balance of passenger quantity led by each guide, which makes
the initial assignment of the guide more reasonable. Moreover, the established multi-objective path optimization method for
the guided crowd can not only get the speciﬁc guidance paths from nodes to nodes but also avoid excessive deviation from
a certain target value. Besides, it can avoid the problem of determining the weight coeﬃcient of multiple inﬂuence factors.
The life safety of every passenger is very important. The addition of the guide is beneﬁcial to evacuate more passengers
within a certain period of time.
3. Model
The phenomenon of temporary emergency stop at the nearby subway station caused by the fault of the train itself occurs
on occasion [4] . At this time, a nearby train in normal operation will go to the station as a rescue vehicle to tow. Passengers
on the rescue vehicle and on the faulty train will be cleared in order to avoid the re-occurrence of the accident, and this
station will be only outbound and no longer inbound. Besides, when the station facilities fail and there are potential safety
hazards that affect the normal operation, it may also cause temporary passenger clearance of the station. The hybrid method
integrating pedestrian dynamics model, assignment scheme of guide, guide path planning is proposed as shown in Fig. 1
in order to effectively evacuate passengers under guides in the above situations. The social force model driving passenger
movement and the minimum cost model for passenger path selection are ﬁrstly introduced. Then, the determination method
of the number and location of guides is put forward based on the cost function and Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM). Finally,
the evacuation path planning model for guides is established based on the multi-objective optimization method.
This paper makes the following reasonable assumptions in order to simplify the description of the problem as Ref. [2] did.
(1) It is assumed that pedestrians conduct normal inbound and outbound activities for about 360 s before the evacuation
experiment starts [4 8,4 9] .
(2) Guides are professionally trained to understand the internal structure of the subway station. They can receive the
evacuation strategy formulated by the proposed method through the customer terminal equipment and follow the orders.
The guides can quickly reach the designated evacuation starting point at the beginning of evacuation [50] . They can be the
staff in the subway station [2] .
(3) Since the passenger can turn his/her head to observe the rear, it is assumed that the passenger’s vision ﬁeld is a
circle with radius R V [51] . The induction radius of guide is 1.1 times of R V [16] .

3.4. Guide path planning based on multi-objective optimization
When an emergency occurs in the subway station, the main goal of passenger management is to guide passengers to
reach safety areas quickly and safely. It is assumed that emergencies do not affect the use of facilities in the subway station.
On this basis, the initial walking network of passengers is established and abstracted into a directed graph G , G = (N, E) .
Among which, N is the set of evacuation nodes, that is, N = (O, D, W ) . Here, O is the initial node, that is, the guide position

3.5. Model solution
In recent years, more and more advanced algorithms are used to solve multi-objective optimization problems. Pasha
et al. [57] solved the assembly transportation problem between suppliers and manufacturers by using the genetic algorithm
of elitism strategy. Liu et al. [58] solved the multi-objective problem based on the angle selection strategy and the shift
density estimation strategy. Dulebenets et al. [59] developed a heuristic algorithm for solving the pedestrian evacuation path
optimization model with six objectives. Zhao and Zhang [60] used learning automaton to optimize the decomposition-based
multi-objective optimization framework. Fathollahi-Fard et al. [61] introduced two new hybrid meta heuristic algorithms to
solve the tire supply chain network design model in the fuzzy environment. Jain et al. [62] combined crow search algorithm
with particle swarm optimization algorithm to improve the net return of crops and reduce the utilization of fertilizers.
Most improvements were to use another advanced algorithm to optimize the existing algorithms for solving multi-
objective problems which were based on the actual requirements [63,64] . Generally, the algorithms for solving multi-
objective problems can be classiﬁed into Pareto based methods, decomposition based methods and index based methods
according to the selection mechanism [65] . Pareto based method is a very popular and widely used solution method, in
which the most typical algorithm is NSGA-II which can obtain stable solutions [66–68] . NSGA-II could obtain an approxi-
mate Pareto optimal solution through fast non dominated sorting and elitism strategy. It has high operation eﬃciency, good
distribution of solution set, and good performance for low dimensional optimization problems. Therefore, NSGA-II is selected
as the method to solve the multi-objective model in this paper, since there are only two objective functions. The solution
process is listed in Table 3 .
Each step in Table 3 is further explained in details.
Step 1: The subway station scene is abstracted according to the actual data, and the corresponding evacuation network
diagram, distance matrix and capacity matrix are obtained. The positions of passengers in Massmotion are extracted when
they get on and off normally for 6 min. The positions of guides are obtained through the constructed guide assignment
scheme. These location data are imported into NSGA-II algorithm based on MATLAB software platform.
Step 2: Enter constraints in NSGA-II and calculate the evacuation time of each guide. Take the maximum evacuation time
as an objective function and input it. Calculate the sum of the congestion cost of each path taken by each guide as another
objective function and input it.
Step 3: Determine the constraint type. Judge whether the constraint type of the model is nonlinear boundary constraint
according to the input constraint conditions.
Step 4: The initial population is composed of initial individuals, and each individual corresponds to the evacuation path
of guides under a set of constraints. The values of the two objective functions under this path are calculated, respectively.
Step 5: Judge whether the number of iterations reaches the maximum value. If so, get the Pareto solution. If not, judge
whether it is the optimal Pareto solution. If the optimal solution condition is satisﬁed, the Pareto solution is obtained. If not,
proceed to Step 6. Note that the optimal solution condition is that all individuals in the ﬁrst non dominated front in recent
generations are the same.
Step 6: Operations such as coding, selection, split crossover and split mutation are performed for the existing parent
population to produce the child population. Calculate the evacuation time and congestion cost under the child population
corresponding to the guide evacuation path.
Step 7: Merge parent and child populations. The non dominated sorting and the congestion distance calculation of all
individuals in the combined population are conducted. In the process of non dominated sorting, the concept of rank is
used to represent the non dominated level of each individual. The distance between an individual in a front-end and other
individuals in this front-end is deﬁned as the congestion distance, which is used to characterize the congestion degree
between individuals.

The presence of the guide can calm the panic and anxiety especially for some passengers who are not familiar with
the station environment and avoid the occurrence of secondary accidents. Guide assignment scheme and evacuation path
planning of guided passengers are proposed in this paper, which can improve the evacuation eﬃciency of subway stations
in emergency. It could also provide decision support for managers to formulate evacuation strategies, and further improve
the service level of the station. It is suggested to arrange the guide at the key positions, such as stairs/escalators, gates, etc.,
so as to facilitate the guide to reach the designated position faster in case of emergency. At the same time, the guide shall
be equipped with loudspeakers and wear eye-catching clothes to expand the transmission range of guidance information. In
addition, it is suggested that managers organize more daily evacuation drills to train a group of staffs who are familiar with
the internal structure of the subway station. Furthermore, the staffs should skillfully use the customer terminal equipment
to obtain guidance path information.
6. Conclusion
The addition of the guide has an obvious effect on improving the evacuation eﬃciency, which is an important means
of safety control in the subway station. The existing research on the guidance strategy is often based on a simple scenario
and only considers the guide’s choice of exit, ignoring the possible congestion on the path. This paper proposes a guidance
strategy in emergency aiming at both guide assignment scheme and evacuation path planning. Comprehensively considering
the factors of passenger confusion index, the number of guides, labor cost and the balance of passenger quantity led by
each guide, a method to determine the initial number and location of guides is proposed based on the cost function and

model based on multi-objective optimization is proposed. Using the evacuation time as the objective function can ensure
more passengers leave the station as soon as possible. Using the congestion cost as the other objective function can avoid
the excessive congestion on some paths and reduce the secondary injury caused by stampede, etc. Taking Qingdao Jimiya
subway station as an example, it is veriﬁed that the social force model can be used to describe the movement behavior
of passengers by comparing the data of outbound passengers’ walking time, and the minimum cost model can reﬂect the
path selection behavior rule of passengers by comparing the data of the number of inbound passengers passing through the
gates. Simulation results indicate that the travel purpose of passengers under guides are stronger, and the total evacuation
eﬃciency can be improved by about 13%. Guided passengers’ choice of escalator, stair and exit is more balanced, which
could avoid passengers choosing the same facility in the same time period due to herding behavior.
However, this study also has some limitations. The guidance strategy may be adjusted according to the travel habits of
passengers in different countries. Trying to obtain the passenger ﬂow data of subway stations in different countries and
mining more inﬂuence factors which may affect the guidance scheme are the main directions of future research work. In
addition, building guidance strategies in the case of other disasters such as ﬂoods, ﬁres and terrorist attacks will be also one
of our main work in the future.
